docs.name: Riverside Allotment Society annual report 2024.md
docs.body:
# Riverside Allotment Society
## Annual report to members, 2023-24 season
Presented at the Annual General Meeting, Saturday 19 October 2024, Ashbourne Vale Community Hall
Prepared by the committee: Gwen Thackeray (Chair), Alan Ferris (Treasurer), Maya Collins (Secretary), Hamid Rostami (Site Warden)

### 1. Chair's introduction

Welcome to our annual report. It has been a season of extremes. A very wet spring left the lower plots near the river waterlogged until the middle of May, and then July brought two heatwaves and a hosepipe ban that lasted most of August. Despite this, the site has never looked better, our waiting list is longer than ever, and members have produced extraordinary harvests. I want to thank everyone who turned up to the work parties, especially those who helped rebuild the shared compost bays and repaint the trading hut.

This report covers membership, the site, finances, events, rules and the plans for next season. Please read it before the AGM so that we can spend the meeting on discussion and decisions rather than reading out numbers.

### 2. Membership

The society has 64 plots on the Riverside site: 38 full plots of about 250 square metres and 26 half plots. All plots were let throughout the season. Eleven plots changed hands during the year, mostly because members moved away or were no longer able to manage the work. We welcomed eleven new plot holders, several of them young families.

The waiting list stands at 47 people, up from 31 last year. The average wait for a half plot is now about two years. To make the site available to more people, the committee proposes that new tenants should normally start on a half plot and can apply to move to a full plot after two seasons.

We carried out plot inspections in May, July and September. Most plots were well cultivated. Six plot holders received a first letter about overgrown or neglected plots and four of those improved. Two tenancies were ended after a second warning and the plots were re-let from the waiting list.

### 3. The site

The main work this year was replacing the water pipe along the central path, which had been leaking for several seasons and was responsible for a large part of our water bill. The new pipe was laid by volunteers over three weekends in March, with the trench dug by a hired mini digger. We also installed four new water troughs with self-closing taps.

The shared compost bays were rebuilt from reclaimed pallets, and there is now a clear system: bay one for fresh material, bay two for turning, bay three for finished compost available to all members. Please do not put perennial weeds, diseased plants or cooked food in the bays.

The trading hut was repainted and its roof felt replaced. The hut sells seed potatoes, onion sets, compost, canes, netting and fertiliser at close to cost price on Sunday mornings from March to June.

The river flooded the lower path twice in January. The Environment Agency has advised that this will happen more often in future, and the committee will look into raised beds for the four lowest plots.

We had two thefts from sheds in the autumn, both of hand tools. The gate code has been changed and a new combination padlock fitted. Please do not share the code with anyone who is not a member.

### 4. Finances

The society's accounts for the year ending 30 September 2024 were prepared by the Treasurer and checked by an independent examiner, Mrs Doreen Walsh. A summary is below and the full accounts are available from the Treasurer on request.

Income for the year was £3,914, made up of plot rents of £2,096, trading hut sales of £1,122, a grant of £500 from the Ashbourne Vale Community Fund towards the water pipe, and £196 from the plant sale and other events.

Expenditure was £4,377. The largest items were the water bill at £1,288, which is lower than last year thanks to the new pipe, the pipe materials and digger hire at £1,140, stock for the trading hut at £986, the land rent paid to the council at £640, insurance at £215, and repairs and sundries at £108.

The society therefore had a deficit of £463 for the year, which was planned and was covered from reserves. Reserves at 30 September 2024 stood at £2,851.

### 5. Plot fees for 2025

The council has told us that the land rent will rise by 8 percent from next year, and water charges are also expected to increase. To keep the society on a sound footing, the committee proposes the following plot fees for the 2025 season, to be voted on at the AGM:

- Full plot: £38 per year (currently £34)
- Half plot: £22 per year (currently £20)
- Concessionary rate for members over 65, students and those receiving income-related benefits: 50 percent of the full rate
- Key deposit for new members: £10, refundable

Fees are due by 31 January 2025. Members can pay by bank transfer, by cash at the trading hut, or in two instalments by arrangement with the Treasurer. Even with this increase, our fees remain among the lowest in the district.

### 6. Events

The spring seed swap in February attracted over 60 people, including many from the waiting list. The plant sale in May raised £142 for society funds. The summer open day in July, combined with the produce show, was the best attended in years. Congratulations to Mr Ferris on plot 15 for winning the heaviest marrow class for the third year running, and to plot 14B for the best beetroot.

The school garden project with Oakridge Primary continued, with Year 2 children visiting twice in the summer term to plant and then harvest potatoes. The children's thank you cards are pinned up in the trading hut.

### 7. Rules and reminders

Bonfires are allowed only between 1 November and 28 February, and only dry woody material may be burned. Please check the wind direction and the neighbouring gardens before lighting.

Hosepipes may only be used to fill water butts or troughs, never left running on beds.

Dogs must be kept on a lead at all times on the site.

Shed and greenhouse heights are limited to 2.2 metres, and new structures need approval from the committee.

Please keep paths next to your plot mown and free of trip hazards.

### 8. Plans for next season

The committee proposes to: build raised beds on the four lowest plots; create a small community plot for members who cannot manage a full plot through illness or age; install a second rainwater harvesting tank on the trading hut; and start a tool library so that members can borrow larger tools such as rotavators and strimmers.

We are also looking for a new Secretary from next October, as Maya will be stepping down to focus on her studies. Please talk to any committee member if you are interested.

### 9. Thanks

Thank you to all members, volunteers, and our partners at the Community Fund, Oakridge Primary School and Larkspur Community Pantry, which received over 300kg of surplus produce from our members this season.

### 10. Minutes of last year's AGM (summary)

The 2023 AGM, held on 21 October 2023, approved the accounts, re-elected the committee, and agreed to spend reserves on replacing the central water pipe. Members asked the committee to look into a shared shed for tools and to publish the waiting list numbers on the noticeboard, both of which have been done. A proposal to allow chickens on plots was discussed and not supported, mainly because of concerns about rats.

### 11. Agenda for the 2024 AGM

1. Apologies for absence
2. Minutes of the 2023 AGM
3. Chair's report
4. Treasurer's report and approval of accounts
5. Vote on plot fees for 2025
6. Proposal: new tenants to start on half plots
7. Proposal: raised beds for the lowest plots
8. Election of officers, including a new Secretary from October 2025
9. Any other business

Voting is by show of hands, one vote per plot. Members who cannot attend may appoint a proxy by email to the Secretary before the meeting.

### 12. Contacts

Chair: Gwen Thackeray, plot 3. Treasurer: Alan Ferris, plot 15. Secretary: Maya Collins, plot 14B. Site Warden: Hamid Rostami, plot 27. The noticeboard by the main gate is updated every fortnight, and the members' message group is the quickest way to report problems on site such as broken taps, fallen fences, or vandalism.

Refreshments will be served after the meeting. Please bring a mug.

Late notice from the committee: the council has confirmed that the land rent increase will take effect from 1 April 2025, so members who settle their fees before 31 January will not be affected by any further change this season. Seed orders for the trading hut close on 15 December; please put your requests in the book by the hut door or send them to the Secretary. The winter work party is on Sunday 1 December from 10am, when we will clear the ditch by the lower path and spread wood chip on the main paths.

# Fluffy pancakes (Saturday morning)

Makes about 10 small American-style pancakes.

## Ingredients
- 200g self-raising flour
- 1 tsp baking powder
- 1 tbsp caster sugar
- pinch of salt
- 2 large eggs
- 250ml milk
- 25g melted butter, plus a little for the pan
- 1 tsp vanilla extract

## Method
1. Whisk the flour, baking powder, sugar and salt in a large bowl.
2. In a jug beat the eggs with the milk, melted butter and vanilla.
3. Make a well in the dry ingredients and pour in the wet mixture, whisking until just smooth. A few lumps are fine. Rest for 5 minutes.
4. Heat a non-stick frying pan over a medium heat and wipe with a little butter.
5. Pour in about 3 tbsp of batter per pancake. Cook for 1 to 2 minutes until bubbles appear on the surface, then flip and cook for another minute.
6. Keep warm in a low oven while you cook the rest.

## To serve
Sliced banana and maple syrup, blueberries and Greek yoghurt, or crispy bacon for Daniel.

Childcare Service (fictional government scheme)

4 September 2024

Ms Maya Collins
Flat 3, 14 Larkspur Row
Ashbourne Vale AV3 9QT

Reference: TFC-0041-77821

Dear Ms Collins,

Your tax-free childcare account for Leo Reyes has been reconfirmed

Thank you for reconfirming your details. You can continue to use your childcare account for Leo for the next three months, until 3 December 2024.

For every £8 you pay into the account, the scheme adds £2, up to £500 every three months (£2,000 a year) for each child. You can use the account to cover approved childcare, including Oakridge Primary's breakfast and after-school clubs and registered holiday clubs.

You must reconfirm your eligibility again by 3 December 2024. To qualify, you and your partner must each expect to earn at least the equivalent of 16 hours a week at the National Minimum Wage, and neither of you can have adjusted net income over £100,000.

Current balance: £412.60
Scheme top-ups this quarter: £96.00

You can sign in to your account at any time to make deposits or pay providers.

Childcare Service
